mainTopic: Identifying the אתרוג, and why certain אתרוגים are פסול
overview: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא that identifies "פרי עץ הדר" as the אתרוג, because its wood tastes like its fruit. It rejects pepper, which also has this feature, because one peppercorn is too small to notice and the Torah wants one fruit. רבי, רבי אבהו and בן עזאי each reread the word הדר to point to the אתרוג: the pen, the fruit that stays on its tree, and the fruit that grows by all water. The גמרא then explains the משנה's rulings. An אתרוג of אשרה or עיר הנדחת is פסול because something set aside for burning counts as crushed. For ערלה, רבי חייא בר אבין and רבי אסי disagree: one says it may not be eaten, and the other says it has no money value. After a challenge from impure תרומה, the גמרא concludes that both require permission to eat, and רבי אסי also requires money value. The difference between them shows up with an אתרוג of מעשר שני according to רבי מאיר. רבי אסי applies the same idea to מצה and חלה. רב פפא asks where the Torah says מצה must be yours, and the answer, a גזרה שוה from the word "לחם", continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The fruit whose tree tastes like its fruit is the אתרוג
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that "פרי עץ הדר" means a tree whose wood and fruit taste the same, and that tree is the אתרוג.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The Sages taught: "Fruit of a beautiful tree" means a tree whose wood and fruit have the same taste. You must say this is the אתרוג.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by bringing a ברייתא that shows where the Torah tells us that the "fruit of a beautiful tree" is the אתרוג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the words "פרי עץ" (fruit of a tree) as hinting that the fruit and the tree are alike. The tree is like the fruit in taste. The only tree it can think of with this feature is the אתרוג tree.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
Fruit of a beautiful tree (the Torah's name for one of the four species)
The taste of its wood and its fruit is the same
You must say (this is the only option)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic source that the מצוה of פרי עץ הדר is specifically the אתרוג. The rest of the sugya tests this identification.

phrases.english: Gemara: The Sages taught:
"Fruit of a beautiful tree" means
a tree whose wood and fruit taste the same
you must say this is the etrog.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא assumes no other tree fits this description.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the פרק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: "פרי עץ הדר" is a tree whose wood and fruit taste alike, and that is the אתרוג.

steps.title: Why not peppers, whose wood also tastes like the fruit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. פלפלין also fit the description, as רבי מאיר teaches about ערלה, so why not say the verse means pepper?
steps.simpleTranslation: And say it means peppers! As it was taught: רבי מאיר would say, from the words "and you shall plant any tree," don't I already know it is a food tree? Why does the verse add "a food tree"? To include a tree whose wood and fruit taste the same, and that is pepper. This teaches that peppers are obligated in ערלה. And ארץ ישראל lacks nothing, as it says, "You shall not lack anything in it."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first step by pointing to another tree that has the same feature, the pepper tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said "you must say it is the אתרוג," as if only one tree fits. But רבי מאיר teaches that the pepper tree also has wood that tastes like its fruit, and that this is why it is obligated in ערלה. So the identification with the אתרוג is no longer automatic. The extra verse is there to show that pepper grows in ארץ ישראל, so it cannot be dismissed as foreign.

keyTerms.meaning: But say instead (opens a challenge with an alternative)
As it was taught in a ברייתא
Why does the verse need to say this?
The ban on a tree's fruit in its first three years
You shall not lack anything in it (the Land)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר's teaching is about ערלה, not about the four species. The גמרא borrows it only to prove that pepper also has "wood that tastes like its fruit."

phrases.english: But say it means peppers!
As it was taught: Rabbi Meir would say:
From what is implied by "and you shall plant any tree,"
don't I know that it is a food tree?
Why does the verse say "a food tree"?
It means a tree whose wood and fruit taste the same.
You must say this is pepper.
This teaches you that peppers are obligated in orlah.
And Eretz Yisrael lacks nothing,
phrases.notes: This explains why pepper is relevant to ערלה, which applies in ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: as it says: "You shall not lack anything in it."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim in step 1 that only the אתרוג fits the description.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's conclusion that "פרי עץ הדר" must be the אתרוג.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Pepper also has wood that tastes like its fruit (according to רבי מאיר), so the description does not single out the אתרוג.

steps.title: Peppers cannot work for the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the verse cannot mean pepper, because there is no workable way to take it.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it cannot mean pepper because it is impossible. How would we do it? If we take one, taking it is not noticeable. If we take two or three, the Torah said one fruit, not two or three fruits. So it is impossible.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that pepper cannot practically be used for the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A single peppercorn is too tiny for anyone to notice it is being held. Taking several would break the rule that the מצוה is one fruit ("פרי" is singular). Since both options fail, the verse must mean the אתרוג.

keyTerms.meaning: Its taking would not be noticeable

steps.whatToRemember: The אתרוג is the only fruit that fits "עץ שטעם עצו ופריו שוה" and can also work as a single, noticeable fruit for the מצוה.

phrases.english: There, it cannot mean pepper, because it is impossible.
How would we do it?
If we take one, its taking is not noticeable.
If we take two or three,
the Torah said one fruit,
and not two or three fruits.
Therefore it is impossible.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical impossibility rules out the alternative
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Pepper fits the taste description just as well as the אתרוג.
steps.terutzMaskana: Pepper cannot be taken as a single, noticeable fruit, so the verse must mean the אתרוג.

steps.title: רבי reads הָדָר as הַדִּיר, the pen
steps.stepSummary: רבי offers a different source. Read הָדָר as הַדִּיר (the pen): just as a flock in a pen has big, small, perfect and blemished animals, so does this tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: Do not read "הָדָר" (beautiful) but "הַדִּיר" (the pen). Just as a pen has large and small, perfect and blemished animals, so too this tree has large and small, perfect and blemished fruits.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי gives a second, separate way to learn from the verse that the fruit is the אתרוג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using the method of אל תקרי, רבי rereads the word הדר as הדיר, a sheep pen. He compares the fruit on the tree to a flock of mixed animals all together in one pen. At this point it is unclear what feature this points to, and the next step questions exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not read it as (a rereading of a word)

phrases.english: Rebbi says:
Do not read "hadar" but "ha-dir" (the pen).

phrases.aramaic: מָה דִּיר זֶה יֵשׁ בּוֹ גְּדוֹלִים וּקְטַנִּים,
phrases.english: Just as this pen has large and small,
perfect and blemished animals,

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי נָמֵי יֵשׁ בּוֹ גְּדוֹלִים וּקְטַנִּים,
phrases.english: so too this tree has large and small,
perfect and blemished fruits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second derivation alongside the ברייתא of step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word הדר hints to הדיר: the tree has fruits of all sizes and qualities together, like a flock in a pen.

steps.title: Don't other fruits also come big, small, and blemished?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי's comparison identifies the אתרוג, since every fruit tree has big, small, perfect and blemished fruits.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say that other fruits don't have large and small, perfect and blemished ones?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי's explanation, because the feature he described seems to fit every fruit tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A source for identifying the אתרוג has to point to something unique about it. Sizes and blemishes are found in all fruit, so as stated so far, רבי's reading proves nothing about the אתרוג.

phrases.english: Is that to say that other fruits don't have
large and small, perfect and blemished ones?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי's explanation from step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's comparison of the tree to a pen of mixed animals.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The feature described is common to all fruit, so it cannot single out the אתרוג.

steps.title: Old and new fruits on the tree together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רבי's real point. On an אתרוג tree, the big fruits from before are still on the tree when the new small ones appear.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what he means: by the time the small ones come, the large ones are still there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining what רבי really meant, which is a feature found only in the אתרוג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison is not about variety in general. It is about different ages living together, like old and young sheep in one pen. אתרוגים stay on the tree from year to year, so new small fruit grow alongside last year's large fruit. Other trees do not hold their fruit that way.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, this is what he means

steps.whatToRemember: רבי's source: the אתרוג is like a pen, since its old large fruits stay on the tree while new small ones grow, which other trees do not do.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what he means:
by the time the small ones come,
the large ones are still there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 by reinterpreting רבי.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי meant that the tree has fruit of mixed sizes and quality, which is true of all trees.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי meant that fruit of different ages exist on the tree at once, which is unique to the אתרוג.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: the fruit that stays on its tree
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו reads הָדָר as הַדָּר, meaning 'that dwells'. The verse means a fruit that stays on its tree from year to year, which is the אתרוג.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: Do not read it הָדָר. Read it הַדָּר, 'that dwells'. It means a fruit that dwells on its tree from year to year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more way to show that פרי עץ הדר means the אתרוג. רבי אבהו reads the word with different vowels so it means 'that dwells'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 explained that big אתרוגים are still on the tree when the new small ones appear. רבי אבהו builds a reading right into the word: הַדָּר means a fruit that 'lives' on its tree across years. Only the אתרוג does this, so the verse points to it.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not read it as… (read the word with different vowels to draw out a teaching)

steps.confusionAlert: אל תקרי does not mean the written word is wrong. The written word stays, and the second reading adds a meaning on top of it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu said:
Do not read 'hadar' (beautiful), but rather 'ha-dar' (that dwells) —
meaning a thing that dwells on its tree from year to year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is another source for the same identification. It is close in idea to the explanation of רבי's view in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הָדָר is read as הַדָּר: a fruit that stays on its tree from year to year, which is the אתרוג.

steps.title: בן עזאי: the fruit that grows on all water
steps.stepSummary: בן עזאי reads הָדָר as אִידוֹר, the Greek word for water. The verse means the fruit that grows by any water, which is the אתרוג.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן עזאי says: Do not read it הָדָר. Read it אִידוֹר, because in Greek water is called אִידוֹר. Which fruit grows on all kinds of water? You must say this is the אתרוג.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one last source. בן עזאי reads the word as the Greek word for 'water'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse is now hinting at a fruit tree that grows on all water (על כל מים). The אתרוג grows on every kind of water source, not only rain or only watering by hand. That makes it the tree the verse means.

keyTerms.meaning: You must say (the answer can only be…)

steps.whatToRemember: There are three readings of הָדָר that identify the אתרוג. רבי reads it as 'pen' (step 4), רבי אבהו as 'dwells', and בן עזאי as 'water'.

phrases.english: Ben Azzai says:
Do not read 'hadar', but rather 'idor',

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן בְּלָשׁוֹן יְווֹנִי קוֹרִין לְמַיִם אִידוֹר,
phrases.english: for in the Greek language they call water 'idor',

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵיזוֹ הִיא שֶׁגָּדֵל עַל כׇּל מַיִם —
phrases.english: and which fruit is it that grows on all waters? —
You must say: this is the etrog.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֶּן עַזַּאי אוֹמֵר: אַל תִּקְרֵי ״הָדָר״, אֶלָּא ״אִידוֹר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a third reading of the same word. It closes the section on where we learn the אתרוג from.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הָדָר is read as אִידוֹר (water): the fruit that grows on all waters, which is the אתרוג.

steps.title: Why is an אתרוג of an אשרה or an עיר הנדחת invalid?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that an אתרוג from an אשרה or an עיר הנדחת is פסול. It asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says an אתרוג from an אשרה or from an עיר הנדחת is פסול. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes its next ruling. It asks why, and this sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a plain question asking for the reason. It is not an attack. Both cases are things the Torah commands us to burn.

keyTerms.meaning: A tree that is worshipped as an idol
A Jewish city led astray into idol worship, which must be burned

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל אֲשֵׁרָה וְשֶׁל עִיר הַנִּדַּחַת — פָּסוּל.
phrases.english: One of an asheirah or of an ir hanidachat is invalid.
What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This starts a new topic. The גמרא returns to the list of rulings in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why an אתרוג from an אשרה or an עיר הנדחת is פסול.

steps.title: It is set for burning, so it counts as ashes
steps.stepSummary: The אתרוג is set aside to be burned. So the law treats it as if it were already crushed to ashes, and it does not have the needed size.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it stands to be burned, its size is considered crushed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אתרוג must be at least a minimum size (שיעור). Something the Torah commands to burn is treated now as if it were already burned to ashes. Ashes have no size, so the אתרוג is missing its שיעור.

keyTerms.meaning: Its size is considered crushed (treated as ashes)

steps.whyThisMatters: כתותי מיכתת שיעוריה is a well-known rule across ש״ס. Anything that must be burned is treated as having no size.

phrases.english: Since it stands to be burned —
its size is considered crushed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the question in step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Something set aside for burning is treated as already crushed. So the אתרוג is missing its required size.

steps.title: Why is an אתרוג of ערלה invalid?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that an אתרוג of ערלה is פסול. It asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says an אתרוג of ערלה is פסול. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next ruling in the משנה and asks why. This sets up a disagreement in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ערלה is fruit from a tree's first three years. It is forbidden to eat and forbidden to get any benefit from. The גמרא asks what exactly makes it פסול, and the next step gives two different answers.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit from a tree's first three years, forbidden to eat or benefit from

phrases.english: And one of orlah is invalid.
What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This moves on to the next ruling in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why an אתרוג of ערלה is פסול.

steps.title: Two reasons: no permission to eat, or no money value
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבין and רבי אסי disagree. One says it is פסול because it may not be eaten. The other says it is פסול because it has no money value.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבין and רבי אסי argue about this. One said: because it may not be eaten. The other said: because it has no money value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with two different reasons given by two אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view says an אתרוג must be a fruit that is allowed to be eaten. The second view says it must have money value, so that it can really be 'yours'. Since benefit from ערלה is forbidden, it is worth nothing and cannot belong to you.
steps.confusionAlert: The 'money value' view is not about the price of the אתרוג. It comes from the word לָכֶם ('for yourselves'), which teaches that the אתרוג must be your own. Something with no value cannot be owned.

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין וְרַבִּי אַסִּי.
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Avin and Rabbi Asi disagree about it.

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ הֶיתֵּר אֲכִילָה,
phrases.english: One said: because it has no permission to be eaten,

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ דִּין מָמוֹן.
phrases.english: and one said: because it has no monetary status.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין וְרַבִּי אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers step 11 with a disagreement.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There are two reasons: it is not allowed to be eaten, or it has no money value.

steps.title: First assumption: each view needs only its own condition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא first assumes each אמורא needs only his own condition. The 'eating' view does not need money value, and the 'money' view does not need permission to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first we think: the one who needs permission to eat does not need money value, and the one who needs money value does not need permission to eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge. It states a first assumption (הוה אמינא) about how the two views differ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This assumption makes the two views fully separate. Under it, a case can fit one view and fail the other. That lets the next step test the 'money' view on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: It enters the mind / we first assume (a first thought that may be dropped later)

steps.confusionAlert: קא סלקא דעתיה signals a first assumption that may later be rejected. Do not treat it as the final conclusion.

phrases.english: It enters the mind (we assume):

phrases.aramaic: מַאן דְּבָעֵי הֶיתֵּר אֲכִילָה לָא בָּעֵי דִּין מָמוֹן,
phrases.english: the one who requires permission to eat does not require monetary status,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאן דְּבָעֵי דִּין מָמוֹן לָא בָּעֵי הֶיתֵּר אֲכִילָה.
phrases.english: and the one who requires monetary status does not require permission to eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This defines how far apart the two views in step 12 are. It prepares the attack in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First assumption: each view requires only its own condition and not the other's.

steps.title: Challenge from impure תרומה: it does have money value
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says an אתרוג of impure תרומה is פסול. That fits the 'eating' view. But by the 'money' view, why is it פסול? A כהן can burn it as fuel under his cooking, so it has value.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: an אתרוג of impure תרומה is פסול. This fits well for the one who says the reason is that it may not be eaten. But for the one who says the reason is that it has no money value, why is it פסול? A כהן burns it under his cooked food!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the 'money value' view using another ruling in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Impure תרומה may not be eaten, so the 'eating' view explains why it is פסול. But a כהן may use it as fuel, so it is useful and has money value. Under the 'money' view as we assumed it in step 13, it should be כשר, yet the משנה says it is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Impure תרומה: forbidden to eat, but a כהן may burn it for fuel
It works well for this view… but for that view (a challenge formula)
He burns it as fuel under his cooking

phrases.english: We learned: one of impure terumah is invalid.
It works well according to the one who says

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ הֶיתֵּר אֲכִילָה — שַׁפִּיר.
phrases.english: 'because it has no permission to be eaten' — fine.
But according to the one who says

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ דִּין מָמוֹן — אַמַּאי?
phrases.english: 'because it has no monetary status' — why is it invalid?
Why, he can burn it under his cooked food!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This uses the assumption from step 13 to challenge the 'money value' view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that an אתרוג of ערלה is פסול because it has no money value.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Impure תרומה has value because it can be used as fuel. The 'money' view, assuming it needs only money value, should then call it כשר. But the משנה says it is פסול.

steps.title: Everyone requires permission to eat; the argument is only about money value
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes its first reading. Both אמוראים agree the אתרוג must be permitted to eat. One also requires money value, and the other does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: about permission to eat, everyone agrees that we need it. Where they argue is about money value. One master holds that we need permission to eat but we do not need money value. The other master holds that we need money value too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the קשיא about impure תרומה by changing how it understands the argument between the two אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 13 the גמרא assumed each view needed only its own condition. Now it says both views need permission to eat, and the 'money' view simply adds a second condition. So impure תרומה is פסול even by the 'money' view, because it may not be eaten, even though it has fuel value.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (signals that the earlier assumption is dropped)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the 'money' view has dropped the eating requirement. It now needs BOTH: permission to eat AND money value.
steps.whyThisMatters: This new reading is the base for everything that follows. The only real argument left is whether money value is needed in addition to permission to eat.

phrases.english: Rather: regarding permission to eat,

steps.title: The difference: an אתרוג of מעשר שני in ירושלים according to רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי מאיר, מעשר שני may be eaten in ירושלים but belongs to Heaven. So it is כשר by the 'eating' view and פסול by the 'money' view.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference is מעשר שני that is in ירושלים, according to רבי מאיר. For the one who said 'because it may not be eaten', this one may be eaten. For the one who said 'because it has no money value', מעשר שני is the property of Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with the needed case: an אתרוג of מעשר שני inside ירושלים, following רבי מאיר's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר שני may be eaten in ירושלים, so the 'eating' view calls it כשר. But רבי מאיר holds that מעשר שני is ממון גבוה, owned by Heaven and not by the person. So it has no money value for him, and the 'money' view calls it פסול.

steps.title: Proof that רבי אסי holds the 'money value' view
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי ruled elsewhere that by רבי מאיר an אתרוג of מעשר שני is פסול. That fits only the 'money' view, so he must be the one who holds it.
steps.simpleTranslation: We can conclude that רבי אסי is the one who said 'because it has no money value'. For רבי אסי said: with an אתרוג of מעשר שני, according to רבי מאיר a person does not fulfill his obligation with it on יום טוב. According to the חכמים, a person does fulfill his obligation with it on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to figure out which אמורא holds which view. It brings a ruling of רבי אסי as a proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 12 we were not told who holds which reason. רבי אסי's ruling matches the 'money' view exactly: by רבי מאיר it is פסול because the person does not own it, and by the חכמים it is כשר. So the 'money' view must be his, and the 'eating' view belongs to רבי חייא בר אבין.

steps.title: The proof is accepted

steps.simpleTranslation: Indeed, conclude this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the proof without any challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now both views have owners. רבי אסי needs permission to eat and also money value. רבי חייא בר אבין needs only permission to eat.
steps.whatToRemember: Both views need permission to eat. רבי אסי also needs money value, so by רבי מאיר an אתרוג of מעשר שני is פסול.

steps.title: רבי אסי's full statement: the אתרוג of מעשר שני
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now quotes רבי אסי's statement in full, starting again with the אתרוג part.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the statement itself. רבי אסי said: with an אתרוג of מעשר שני, according to רבי מאיר a person does not fulfill his obligation with it on יום טוב. According to the חכמים, a person does fulfill his obligation with it on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: With the word גופא, the גמרא turns to study רבי אסי's statement on its own. It repeats the אתרוג part, which leads into the other cases in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Above, only the אתרוג part was quoted, to serve as a proof. Here the גמרא brings the whole statement for its own sake. The repeated אתרוג line opens a list of cases that all depend on one question: does the person own מעשר שני?

steps.mimraCoreRuling: By רבי מאיר an אתרוג of מעשר שני is פסול. By the חכמים it is כשר.

steps.title: The same argument applied to מצה and חלה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי's statement continues. By רבי מאיר, מצה of מעשר שני does not count on פסח, and dough of מעשר שני is exempt from חלה. The חכמים rule the opposite in both cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: With מצה of מעשר שני: according to רבי מאיר a person does not fulfill his obligation with it on פסח. According to the חכמים he does fulfill his obligation with it on פסח. Dough of מעשר שני: according to רבי מאיר it is exempt from חלה. According to the חכמים it must have חלה taken.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי's statement continues with two more cases that follow the same argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each of these cases the law needs the item to belong to the person. רבי מאיר says מעשר שני belongs to Heaven, so it does not count for מצה and is exempt from חלה. The חכמים say it belongs to the person, so it counts for מצה and must have חלה taken.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of dough given to a כהן

steps.whatToRemember: One argument, three results. רבי מאיר holds that מעשר שני is ממון גבוה, so it is not 'yours': it is פסול for אתרוג and מצה, and exempt from חלה. The חכמים hold that it is yours, so all three laws apply.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רבי אסי's 'money value' idea is not a one-time rule about אתרוג. It comes from a broad argument about who owns מעשר שני, and that argument affects several מצוות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי אסי's statement from step 20 with more cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By רבי מאיר, מעשר שני is not the person's own: it does not count for מצה and is exempt from חלה. By the חכמים, it counts for מצה and must have חלה taken.

steps.title: רב פפא asks: where does the תורה say מצה must be yours?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא accepts that the 'yours' rule works for חלה and אתרוג, since the פסוק says "your" for both. But for מצה no such word appears, so why would מצה of מעשר שני not count according to רבי מאיר?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא objected: It makes sense for dough, because it is written "the first of your dough." It also makes sense for the אתרוג, because it is written "for yourselves," meaning from what is yours. But for מצה, is it written "your מצה"?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges part of רבי אסי's ruling. He agrees with the חלה and אתרוג parts, but he asks how we know that מצה must be your own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By רבי מאיר, מעשר שני is Heaven's money, so it is not truly 'yours.' That only matters where the תורה requires ownership. For חלה the word is "עריסותיכם" (your dough) and for אתרוג it is "לכם" (for yourselves), but the מצה verses have no word saying "your," so there seems to be no reason for מצה of מעשר שני to be פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: He strongly objected to it, a challenge to the previous statement
Granted / it makes sense (for these cases)
The first of your dough, the פסוק that commands חלה
For yourselves, from the אתרוג פסוק
Your מצה, a word the תורה does NOT use

steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא is not arguing on the חלה or אתרוג rulings. He accepts them completely. His question is only about מצה.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa strongly objected to this:
Granted, regarding dough,
it is written: "The first of your dough."
phrases.notes: "Your" dough means dough that belongs to you, and מעשר שני by רבי מאיר is not yours.

phrases.english: The etrog too: it is written "for yourselves,"
meaning from your own.
But matzah,
is it written "your matzah"?
phrases.notes: He's asking it rhetorically: the verse never says "your matzah," so why should ownership matter?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the מצה part of רבי אסי's ruling quoted in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אסי's ruling that by רבי מאיר, מצה of מעשר שני does not count on פסח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'not yours' reasoning only works where a פסוק requires ownership. חלה and אתרוג have such a word, but מצה does not.

steps.title: מצה is linked to חלה through the shared word 'bread'
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שמואל (or רב יימר בר שלמיא) answers with a גזרה שוה. "לחם" appears by מצה and also by חלה, so the 'yours' requirement of חלה applies to מצה too. This passage ends as the second פסוק is about to be quoted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר שמואל said, and some say it was רב יימר בר שלמיא: It is learned from "bread" and "bread." It is written here, "bread of affliction," and it is written there…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב פפא's question. It says מצה learns the ownership rule from חלה because both are called "לחם" (bread).
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזרה שוה connects two topics that share a word, so a rule stated in one applies to the other. מצה is called "לחם עני" (bread of affliction), and the חלה section also uses "לחם." Because of this link, the word "your" written by חלה also teaches that מצה must be yours, so מעשר שני, which is Heaven's by רבי מאיר, does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (a different name for who said it)
It comes / it is learned from
A teaching that links two topics through a shared word
Bread of affliction, the תורה's name for מצה
Here / there, the two places being compared

steps.confusionAlert: The word "your" is not written by מצה itself. It is borrowed from חלה through the shared word "לחם."
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how רבי אסי's ruling can stand. Without this link, there would be no source for saying that מצה must belong to you.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Shmuel said,
and some say it was Rav Yeimar bar Shelamya:
It is derived from "bread" and "bread."
phrases.notes: This is a גזרה שוה built on the shared word "לחם."

phrases.english: It is written here, by matzah: "bread of affliction,"
and it is written there, by challah…
phrases.notes: The answer continues on the next amud, where the חלה פסוק with "לחם" is quoted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge from step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Provides a scriptural source through a גזרה שוה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the מצה פסוק does not say "your," ownership should not matter for מצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Through "לחם"–"לחם," מצה shares חלה's 'yours' requirement, so מעשר שני מצה does not count by רבי מאיר.
